efet_title: Media Statement: Deli Hummus range Product Safety Recall - The National Consumer Commission
efet_body:
Media Statement: Deli Hummus range Product Safety Recall
Date Posted:
October 3, 2024
On 16 September 2024, Shoprite Checkers notified the Consumer Commission (NCC) of a product recall of the Deli Hummus range manufactured by BM Foods (a member of Sea Harvest Group), following the detection of Listeria Monocytogenes which is a species of foodborne bacteria.
The affected products are the Deli Hummus range, specifically the following:
Traditional Hummus (125g and 300g);
Reduced Fat Hummus (125g);
Zataar Hummus (125g and 300g);
Red Pepper Hummus (125g and 300g); and
Caramelised Onion Hummus (125g).
The respective sell-by dates of the products are 10 September 2024 to 08 October 2024.
Subsequent to the product recall notification, and in line with Section 60 of the Consumer Protection Act 68 of 2008, Shoprite Checkers has now provided an interim Investigation Report to the NCC on the Deli Hummus range. The preliminary findings of the report point to some areas of concern on product handling at the manufacturing level, however, the NCC awaits a final report from Shoprite Checkers. Parallel to the said in-house processes, the NCC is independently investigating the recalled products on identified operational issues that pertain to food safety.
The NCC’s Acting Commissioner, Mr. Hardin Ratshisusu, urged consumers to immediately stop consuming the products and return same to the supplier for a full refund with or without any proof of purchase. He further added that “at this stage, the NCC is not able to determine the extent of the distribution of the products as this is the subject of an investigation. Suppliers are urged not to distribute these products further until the investigation is finalised.”
The NCC is monitoring this recall based on the Product Recall provisions of the Consumer Protection Action read with the product recall safety guidelines.
ENDS
Issued by: National Consumer Commission (NCC)

news_title: Product safety recall – Groovy Baby ‘I Spy a Fly’ board book - The National Consumer Commission (NCC)
efet_title: Product safety recall - Groovy Baby ‘I Spy a Fly’ board book - The National Consumer Commission
efet_body:
Product safety recall – Groovy Baby ‘I Spy a Fly’ board book
Date Posted:
September 4, 2026
The National Consumer Commission (NCC) notifies consumers about a product recall as notified by Make Believe Ideas Ltd (MBI). The recall affects one hundred and twenty (120) units, which were sold nationally from February 2025 to August 2026.
According to MBI, the Groovy Baby ‘I Spy a Fly’ board book (ISBN-13: 9781836422600) may, in some instances, have the fly’s wings on the last page detach when pulled, posing a potential choking hazard. The affected books have a green frog with orange netting on the front cover. The final page shows a purple fly with googly eyes and four iridescent plastic wings. The book is marked for ages 0+.
Consumers are urged to immediately stop using the book, pull the wings off the last page, cut each wing into four pieces and take a photograph of the 16 pieces on or adjacent to the last page, before disposing of the pieces in a bin that is inaccessible to children and sending the photograph to MBI for a full refund.
Questions relating to this recall may be directed to:
ProductRecall@thencc.org.za
.

news_title: Product safety recall – Certain 2026 – 2027 Ford Ranger double cab vehicles - The National Consumer Commission (NCC)
efet_title: Product safety recall - Certain 2026 – 2027 Ford Ranger double cab vehicles - The National Consumer Commission
efet_body:
Product safety recall – Certain 2026 – 2027 Ford Ranger double cab vehicles
Date Posted:
August 30, 2026
The National Consumer Commission (NCC) informs consumers of a product safety recall issued by Ford Motor Company of Southern Africa (Pty) Ltd (Ford). The recall affects 2 275 (Two Thousand Two Hundred and Seventy-five) Ford Ranger Double Cab vehicles produced for the 2026-2027 production year. The affected vehicles were sold nationwide between 22 May 2026 and 23 June 2026 through Ford franchised dealers and were also exported to Namibia, Botswana, Lesotho and Eswatini.
According to the supplier, the side curtain airbags of the affected vehicles may interact with the B-Pillar trim during inflation and not deploy as intended. If this occurs, the B-Pillar ramp may detach from the vehicle and plunge (become a projectile) when the side curtain airbag deploys. The detachment of the B-Pillar ramp may increase the risk of injury to vehicle occupants during deployment of the side curtain airbag.
Consumers who own the affected vehicles are urged to take their vehicles to the nearest authorised Ford dealership to arrange for an inspection and repair. Any remedial work will be carried out at no cost to the consumer.
“This recall affects a safety-critical component of a significant number of vehicles. Owners or users of these vehicles should contact the supplier without delay. The NCC will be monitoring this and other recalls to ensure all affected vehicles in South Africa are attended to”, said Acting Commissioner, Hardin Ratshisusu.
Questions relating to this recall may be directed to:
ProductRecall@thencc.org.za
.

efet_body:

Selected Toyota models have been recalled over an instrument-display fault that could prevent drivers from seeing important vehicle warnings. Photo: Stock.
Toyota drivers have been urged to check whether their vehicles are affected by a recall involving 518 cars sold across South Africa.
The recall affects selected Toyota RAV4 PHEV, Corolla Cross, Corolla Hatchback, Crown and GR Corolla vehicles.
The
National Consumer Commission
(NCC) announced the recall after Toyota South Africa Motors notified it.
According to the NCC, the recall relates to a programming problem affecting the combination meter. This system displays warning and indicator lights, gauges and other vehicle messages on the 12.3-inch instrument screen.
The affected vehicles include:
16 RAV4 PHEV vehicles built from July 8, 2024 onwards
Four Corolla Cross vehicles built from July 2, 2024 onwards
391 Corolla Hatchback vehicles built from October 7, 2022 onwards
21 Crown vehicles built from October 17, 2022 onwards
86 GR Corolla vehicles built from February 16, 2023 onwards
Not every vehicle built after these dates is necessarily affected. Owners should contact an authorised Toyota dealership and provide their vehicle identification number, or VIN, to confirm whether their particular car is included.
The NCC said unnecessary data may be repeatedly written to a memory device because the combination meter was improperly programmed.
This could cause the device to deteriorate sooner than intended and may cause the instrument display to fail to show information when the vehicle is started.
Should another vehicle malfunction occur while the display is not working, the driver may not see the relevant warning or indicator light.
A notification may appear on the vehicle’s central multimedia screen. However, motorists who do not notice it could continue driving without realising a vehicle malfunction.
“Depending on the malfunction, continued driving may increase the risk of an accident,” the NCC warned.
Acting NCC commissioner Hardin Ratshisusu urged consumers to take recall notices seriously and ensure affected vehicles are presented to the manufacturer for the necessary work.
The repair involves reprogramming the combination meter assembly and will be carried out free of charge at an authorised Toyota dealership.
Vehicle recalls have increased sharply in South Africa in recent years.
According to NCC figures reported by
Wanted Online
, recall campaigns increased from 25 during the 2023/24 financial year to 35 in 2024/25, before rising to 75 in 2025/26.
Mechanical and physical faults involving engines, transmissions, brakes, steering systems, airbags and fuel systems still account for most recalls. However, an increasing number now involve software, electronic control units and digital displays.
NCC spokesperson Phetho Ntaba told the publication the increase could indicate greater transparency rather than deteriorating vehicle quality, as manufacturers identify defects and notify consumers earlier.
Toyota corporate communications manager Refilwe Ramatlhodi Ndhlovu said recall and service campaigns form an important part of the manufacturer’s commitment to quality, durability and reliability.
Modern vehicles contain numerous electronic control units and millions of lines of software code, meaning faults can sometimes affect every vehicle using the same programming.
Owners of the affected Toyota models should contact their nearest authorised dealership with their 17-character VIN and arrange the free repair if required.
The VIN can ordinarily be found on the vehicle’s licence disc, registration documents or identification plate.
Toyota South Africa’s customer contact centre can be reached on
0800 139 111
. Recall-related enquiries may also be sent to the NCC at
ProductRecall@thencc.org.za
.
